source.title: Surrogate Gap Minimization Improves Sharpness-Aware Training
source.authors: Juntang Zhuang; Boqing Gong; Liang-Zhe Yuan; Yin Cui; Hartwig Adam; N. Dvornek; S. Tatikonda; James S. Duncan; Ting Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own tests of whether minimizing a sharpness-related surrogate gap changes held-out accuracy, using a different sharpness measure from V7.
record.gate_note: The paper's central experiments compare GSAM, SAM, and vanilla training on image-classification accuracy. It also reports a ViT-B/32 sweep over α that relates estimated and measured dominant Hessian eigenvalues to test accuracy. Hyperparameter searches and results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization premise to develop GSAM and evaluates its performance. Its surrogate gap and unscaled Hessian eigenvalue do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rank train–test gaps. No other listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: they propose the surrogate gap as a tractable sharpness measure and report that GSAM improves performance across architectures. The negligible computational overhead is relative to SAM; both require approximately twice vanilla training's computation per step. Their theoretical claims concern convergence and improved generalization under stated assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains with GSAM, which adds an orthogonal ascent step to SAM to minimize a surrogate gap; its reported datasets and accuracy comparisons do not reproduce the claim versions' specified experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: For ViT-B/32, the paper reports that varying α changes estimated and measured dominant eigenvalues and test accuracy. Data augmentation and base optimizer are also varied in supplementary comparisons, with results primarily presented in figures.

fits_no_version.finding: For ViT-B/32, GSAM improves over SAM on all five recorded ImageNet evaluations; ImageNet-v1 accuracy increases from 73.6% to 76.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GSAM can improve image-classification accuracy over SAM using an additional orthogonal ascent step.

fits_no_version.finding: The α sweep reports higher test accuracy alongside lower dominant Hessian eigenvalues, and surrogate-gap estimates match measured eigenvalues in trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested ViT-B/32 settings, surrogate-gap minimization reduces unscaled curvature while improving test accuracy, and the surrogate gap provides a curvature proxy.

record.problems: The empirical results are image-classification accuracy comparisons, not direct measurements of train-test error gaps. The α and eigenvalue trends in Figure 4 are figure-only; the measured eigenvalues are computed on a subset. The authors say standard deviation is typically negligible (< 0.1%) compared to the improvements, but do not give uncertainty for each table entry.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports additional model-by-dataset-by-method results, and Table 3 reports transfer results. These were not extracted because they do not test a listed version and the selected ViT-B/32 rows suffice to document the paper's distinct surrogate-gap finding; Figures 5–9 and Tables 2, 5, and 6 also contain further method comparisons or ablations not needed for the mapped claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity; MLP-Mixer comparisons do not isolate this claim.
Adaptive methods versus SGD under comparable tuning on the same architecture. Different base optimizers are assigned to different architecture families.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: R1–R5 document the study's own method performance rather than claim-test results. Their descriptive accuracy improvements are real, but cannot establish any listed version. The text's broad claim of consistent improvement has exceptions: Table 1 reports lower GSAM accuracy than SAM for ResNet-50 on ImageNet-R and ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-C.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

The paper compares vanilla SGD and AdamW in its experiments, but does not test the stated adaptive-optimizer generalization gap under limited tuning or report training performance for that comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.

The study uses a surrogate gap and dominant Hessian eigenvalue, not the magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measure in V7; it does not compare train-test gaps among networks with similarly low training loss.

conditions.value: varied; specific plotted values not recoverable from text

rows.measure: ImageNet top-1 accuracy and dominant Hessian eigenvalue
rows.note: Text says increasing α decreases the dominant value and improves test accuracy; the displayed values are figure-only.
rows.check: Section 6.2 reports improved test accuracy and lower dominant eigenvalues as α increases at fixed ρ. This measures neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor train–test gaps, and uses a transformer rather than V7's convolutional family. Figure 4 uses constant ρ, unlike the main experiments' decayed schedule.

rows.check: Agreement in trend between a surrogate-gap estimate and power-iteration eigenvalues validates a proxy for unscaled curvature; it does not test V7's generalization-gap ranking. The estimates use the full training set, whereas measured eigenvalues use a subset.
